inline_comments.comment: Same issue as the `togglePanel` open-path above: the `Promise<boolean>` returned by `focusOnUIElement` is silently dropped with no `.then()` handler or fallback. Add a `.then(success => { if (success === false) document.body.focus(); })` to be consistent with how the close-path is handled in the same `toggleNav` branch (lines 401–410).

The `showPanel` function is declared `async` but contains no `await` expression. The `focusOnUIElement` call on the next line fires a `Promise<boolean>` that is neither awaited nor returned, meaning it is completely decoupled from the `Promise<void>` that `async` implicitly wraps the function body in. Callers cannot observe focus completion. Either drop the `async` keyword (since the function has become fire-and-forget) or `await` the `focusOnUIElement` call and handle the result so the caller can act on success/failure.

`focusOnUIElement` is invoked with `poll: true`, which means it returns a `Promise<boolean>` when the first synchronous focus attempt fails. That promise is neither awaited nor has `.catch()` attached. While the implementation resolves rather than rejects, the `false` resolution (focus polling timed out) is silently ignored with no fallback. Consider awaiting the result and falling back to `document.body.focus()` on failure, matching the pattern used in `shortcuts.ts`.

`showSidebar` is still declared `async` but no longer contains an `await` expression. The internal `focusOnUIElement` promise is detached from the outer async wrapper, so the function effectively returns `Promise<void>` that resolves immediately while focus polling continues in the background. Drop the `async` keyword to accurately reflect the fire-and-forget nature of this function, or restore `await` and handle the result.

Same dropped-promise issue as `addons.tsx`: `focusOnUIElement` with `poll: true` returns a `Promise<boolean>` that is discarded. A `false` resolution (focus failed after polling) produces no fallback behavior and no observable signal to the caller.

Three lines of commented-out code (`// if (success) { ... }`) were left in without any `TODO` or explanatory note. Per project conventions, commented-out code blocks must either be removed or accompanied by a clearly actionable comment explaining why the code is disabled and when it should be re-enabled. If the landmark animation is intentionally removed, delete these lines.

general_comments.comment: There is a systematic inconsistency in how the `Promise<boolean>` from `focusOnUIElement` (with `poll: true`) is handled across the three changed files. In `shortcuts.ts`, the **close** path explicitly chains `.then(success => { if (success === false) document.body.focus(); })`, but the new **open** paths in both `togglePanel` and `toggleNav` simply discard the promise. In `addons.tsx` and `menu.tsx` the promise is also dropped. A consistent pattern — either always attach a `.then()` fallback or define a shared wrapper that handles the fallback — would make the behavior predictable and easier to maintain.
